subject.title: [Bug] Docker sandbox container name collision across multiple instances on same host

question: Should OpenClaw scope non-shared sandbox runtime identity by resolved workspace/HOME now, and what upgrade cleanup behavior should old scope-key runtimes receive?
rationale: The source-backed bug is clear, but the permanent key shape and one-time reset affect sandbox reuse, persisted runtime state, and the security boundary between co-hosted instances.

options.title: Scope by workspace and document cleanup
options.body: Proceed with the active workspace-scoping direction and require tests plus release-note or Doctor guidance for old non-shared containers and workspaces.

options.title: Fail closed on detected mismatch
options.body: Keep current names but reject reuse when existing runtime labels/config do not match the current workspace, trading compatibility for explicit operator action.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle design
options.body: Pause the narrow fix if maintainers want sandbox lifecycle work to define one combined identity and cleanup contract first.

recommendation.title: Scope by workspace and document cleanup
recommendation.body: Proceed with the active workspace-scoping direction and require tests plus release-note or Doctor guidance for old non-shared containers and workspaces.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sandbox security/product history and authored the adjacent sandbox lifecycle direction referenced by this issue.
